title: footgun: 'cat' claims to 'Display file contents' for any file and the fs layer treats .cvs as a supported semantic file stored as text.
detail: vfs.readFile returns ModuleCartridge|null and discards any string value (FileSystem.base.ts:57 requires typeof!=='string', line 66 returns null for disk text), so `cat <file>.cvs` always reports 'not found' even when the .cvs file exists in the VFS. cat can never show a .cvs (text) file.

title: footgun: 'rm' confirms existence with `const exists = await vfs.readFile(filename)` before deleting, implying it works for any file.
detail: vfs.readFile returns null for text (.cvs) files (FileSystem.base.ts:66), so `rm <file>.cvs` returns 'File not found' and refuses to delete a .cvs file that actually exists in the VFS.

title: footgun: Success message 'Successfully saved to source' and description 'Dump a VFS file to disk' present save as a generally-available persistence action.
detail: vfs.saveToDisk POSTs to the /__editor/save dev middleware and reads via getDiskWritePath; that endpoint only exists under the Vite dev editor plugin. In a production build the fetch hits a non-existent route and save throws / fails; the operation is dev-only, not a real 'save to source'.

title: footgun: handleMakeFile builds a `.cvs` template as the string '# Cave script\n' (line 63) and writes it, and the value is cast `template as ModuleCartridge`.
detail: vfs.writeFile is typed for ModuleCartridge objects; the .cvs string is persisted, but because readFile never returns strings, the just-created .cvs file is subsequently invisible to cat/rm and is dropped by fs-save. The `as ModuleCartridge` cast hides that a string is being stored under an object-typed API.

title: footgun: smartPathUtils imports getFileSuggestions from ./fileUtils (line 2) and getMultipartSuggestions appears to delegate depth-0 completion to it.
detail: A local function getFileSuggestions(token, context) is declared at line 110 and shadows the import; the fileUtils import is unused, and the local one takes (string, context) whereas the imported one takes (string[]). The imported symbol is dead and the two same-named functions have incompatible signatures.

title: footgun: projectRoots() derives project roots by scanning fileCache for manifest paths.
detail: fileCache is populated by refreshFileCache which strips /.cave-dir directory markers but keeps 'manifest.json' entries; however fileCache is only asynchronously refreshed and is clobbered with raw, unfiltered keys by `ls` (lsCommand.ts:14), so project-load/create autocomplete silently reflects a stale or marker-polluted view depending on prior commands.

title: fs-save silently drops every .cvs file
detail: handleFsSave reads each VFS file with `vfs.readFile(file)` then `if (data == null) continue;`. readFile returns null for .cvs (text) files, so .cvs scripts are never written back to disk. fs-load writes .cvs as text (line 77-79) but fs-save cannot round-trip them: cave-script edits made in the VFS are lost on save with no error.

title: ls pollutes and desynchronizes the autocomplete cache with directory markers
detail: vfs.listFiles() returns all keys including '.cave-dir' directory markers (FileSystem.base.listFiles = db.getAllKeys, no filtering). ls overwrites fileCache with these raw files, whereas refreshFileCache deliberately filters markers (fileUtils.ts:33). After `ls`, file autocomplete for cat/rm/save offers '.cave-dir' marker entries until the next refreshFileCache, and ls output itself lists the internal markers to the user.

title: project-duplicate targets a raw folder named after arbitrary project-name text
detail: targetRoot is set to the trimmed new-name string verbatim (`const targetRoot = newName`) and used directly as a path prefix for writeFile(`${targetRoot}/manifest.json`). A name containing spaces, slashes, or '..' becomes part of VFS keys unsanitized, producing malformed or path-traversing keys; unlike other commands here the target is never run through normalize().

title: Shared workspace/linker/gatekeeper singletons created at module load
detail: ModuleLinker, WorkspaceService, RefactorService and Gatekeeper are instantiated once at import time bound to the global vfs. All project commands share this mutable state (moduleCache, activeCartridge). Concurrent or interleaved project-load/close operations race on shared state, and there is no reset path other than closeProject; a failed load can leave activeCartridge/moduleCache inconsistent for later commands.

title: getMultipartSuggestions depth dispatch indexes an array that omits depth 0
detail: depthHandlers has undefined at index 0 and handlers for indices 1-3; `depthHandlers[segments.length]?.(...)` returns [] for any path deeper than 3 segments (index >= 4 is undefined). Combined with the module having no non-test importer, this rich virtual-path completion is dead code whose deepest levels silently no-op.

title: project-save-blueprint version bump can silently no-op
detail: After a successful write, `if (manifestPath)` guards stageProjectVersionInVfs. workspaceService.getManifestPath() returning falsy (no active/loaded project) skips the version bump entirely with a success result, so a saved blueprint can persist without its project version being incremented, breaking the assumption that every save stages a patch.

title: silent failure: empty-catch
detail: Benign-by-intent but undeclared: refreshFileCache().catch swallows any VFS listFiles rejection with only a comment 'Silent failure for autocomplete cache'. If the VFS is persistently broken, autocomplete silently shows a stale/empty list with no user signal; no pdd-ignore marker.

title: silent failure: ignored-return
detail: Real: inside handleFsLoad's Promise.all, each per-file read does `if (!res.ok) return;` — a failed read of an individual file is skipped silently, yet the command still reports `Loaded ${files.length} file(s)` counting files that were never actually written. Partial loads masquerade as full success.

title: silent failure: ignored-return
detail: Real: same pattern as fs-load — `if (!res.ok) return;` per file, then reports `Hard-reloaded ${files.length} file(s)`. After destructively wiping the entire VFS (line 20), any file that fails to re-read is silently missing while the success message claims the full count, so data loss is reported as success.

title: silent failure: fire-and-forget
detail: Mostly benign: refreshFileCache() is invoked without await (it returns a promise resolved internally). rm returns success before the autocomplete cache is actually rebuilt; a rejection is swallowed by refreshFileCache's own catch, so the deleted file can linger in autocomplete briefly. Same fire-and-forget pattern in makeCommands.ts:108/130 and bootstrapLoadCommand.ts:18.

title: silent failure: unchecked-exit
detail: Real: handleProjectClose calls `await workspaceService.closeProject()` with no try/catch; if closeProject rejects, the registry's outer catch reports a generic 'Execution failed', but context.runtime?.unload() and ui?.closeWorkspace() (lines 118-119) are then never reached, leaving runtime/UI in a half-open state. Unlike the other project handlers, close has no local error handling.

title: silent failure: ignored-return
detail: Partial: handleFsSave returns an error on the first failed /__editor/save (line 124-128) but files already written before the failure remain on disk, and any file whose VFS data is null (all .cvs) is skipped via `continue` (line 117) and excluded from the reported saved count — a half-completed save reported without indicating which files were skipped.
